previous_description: An artifact that provides verifiable proof of an action or event for non-repudiation and audit purposes. Anchored to NIST SP 800-53 AU-10 (Non-repudiation), evidence types range from cryptographic signatures to plain audit log entries, with strength characterizing the assurance level per NIST SP 800-63-3.
definition: A kind of proof artifact — log record, digital signature, trusted timestamp, hash, certificate or audit trail — produced or retained by the system so that a specific action or event can later be verified as having occurred and attributed to an actor. It is the artifact itself as a modelled category, not the obligation to produce it or the logging configuration that emits it.

distinguish_from.when: the code configures which events are logged, verbosity, payload inclusion or field sanitisation rather than defining a specific proof artifact and its origin
the element states who must prove an action took place and whether that proof is challengeable, rather than the artifact that constitutes the proof
the concern is how long evidence or logs are kept, where they are archived and how they are destroyed
the element is a control such as signing middleware or a tamper-detection mechanism that mitigates a threat, rather than the record it produces

standard_reference: NIST SP 800-53 AU-10 Non-repudiation (with AU-3 Content of Audit Records)
code_evidence: code that computes and persists a digital signature or HMAC over a transaction or request payload alongside the record (e.g. a signature column, JWS detached signature, or signed receipt object)
an append-only or hash-chained audit trail table, WORM bucket or ledger write (e.g. an audit_events table with previous_hash, AWS QLDB, S3 Object Lock) recording actor, action and timestamp
calls to an RFC 3161 timestamping authority or certificate-based signing service (e.g. TSA client, KMS Sign API, X.509 cert attached to a document approval)
notes: The strength enum mixes an ordinal scale (strong/moderate/weak) with a mechanism ('cryptographic'), which overlaps the type enum; consider separate scales. SP 800-63-3 defines authenticator/identity assurance, not evidence strength, so the citation is loose. 'source' as a required string conflicts with sibling 'source' attributes that are source-code reference objects; consider renaming to 'origin'.
